intake.raw_text:
Client: Marcus Reyes
DOB: 04/11/1991
Provider: Adrian Dai
Appointment: Individual appointment on May 4, 2026
1:30 pm - 2:20 pm CT, 50 min
Billing code: 90834 - Psychotherapy, 45 min
[BPS] Intake Assessment
1. Presenting Problem:
"I fell at home and my brother brought me to the ED. They said I was withdrawing."
2. Signs and Symptoms (DSM-V-TR based) resulting in impairment(s):
(Include current examples for treatment planning, e.g., social, occupational, affective, cognitive, physical)
Patient meets DSM-5-TR criteria for Alcohol Use Disorder, severe (≥6 criteria endorsed: tolerance, withdrawal, hazardous
use, continued use despite social/occupational consequences, time spent obtaining/using, unsuccessful cut-down
attempts); Sedative-Hypnotic Use Disorder, severe (alprazolam); and Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent, moderate
(anhedonia, depressed mood, sleep disturbance, fatigue, appetite change, low self-worth, poor concentration,
psychomotor change — PHQ-9 = 18, moderately severe). Current alcohol withdrawal syndrome with tremor, sweats,
anxiety, insomnia (CIWA-Ar = 12). Resulting impairment spans: occupational (job loss 6 wks ago for intoxication at work),
social (isolation from former sober peers), affective (severe anxiety GAD-7 = 15, depression PHQ-9 = 18), physical
(witnessed fall, uncontrolled HTN, alcohol-related hepatic injury), and cognitive (poor concentration, impaired
insight/judgment on MSE).
3. History of Presenting Problem
(Events, precipitating factors, or incidents leading to need for services):
34yo male with 4-year history of heavy alcohol use and 18-month history of daily alprazolam (originally prescribed for
anxiety, now obtained illicitly), presenting 36 hours after last drink with tremor, sweats, sleep <2h, and a witnessed fall at
home. Referred from ED for medically monitored withdrawal management after CIWA-Ar of 12 on arrival. Lost employment
6 weeks prior due to intoxication at work; DUI charge pending. Ambivalent about treatment ("I'm here because my brother
said so").
Frequency/duration/severity/cycling of symptoms:
Alcohol: 4 years of escalating daily use, currently ~14 standard drinks/day. Alprazolam: 18 months of daily use, escalated
from a legitimate 0.5 mg PRN prescription to illicit 1 mg daily. Cannabis: recreational, 2–3x weekly. Acute alcohol withdrawal
currently moderate (CIWA-Ar = 12). Benzodiazepine withdrawal anticipated but not yet manifest. Depressive and anxious
symptoms have been continuously present x 4 years with worsening since job loss 6 weeks ago.
Was there a clear time when Sx worsened?
Yes — substance use and depressive symptoms escalated sharply 6 weeks ago following job loss (terminated for
intoxication at work). Acute withdrawal began approximately 36 hours prior to admission after a forced cut-down attempt
(no alcohol available at home over the weekend).
Family mental health history:
Father with alcohol use disorder; mother with depression
4. Current Family and Significant Relationships
Strengths/support:: Brother Daniel willing to engage; provided transportation to ED.
Stressors/problems:: Brother is an active substance user (alcohol, cannabis). Patient is housing-dependent on the brother.
No partner, no children. Parents live out of state; minimal contact.
Recent changes:: Job loss 6 weeks ago; pending DUI charge. Brother delivered ultimatum about housing.
Changes desired:: Stable sober housing; restored autonomy; reconnect with mother.
Comment on family circumstances:: Father with untreated alcohol use disorder. Mother with treated major depression.
Patient is the younger of two siblings.
5. Childhood/Adolescent History
(Developmental milestones, past behavioral concerns, environment, abuse, school, social, mental
health)
Normative early development. Raised in two-parent household until parental separation at age 11. First alcohol use at age
16 (family setting, moderate). First cannabis at age 17 (peer setting). High school graduate; completed 18 credits at
community college. No documented abuse or neglect. 2019 MVA at age 28 with mild TBI — brief LOC, evaluated and
discharged from ED. No documented cognitive sequelae, but patient reports lingering difficulty with sustained
concentration since.
6. Social Relationships
Strengths/support:: Brother Daniel (limited — actively using). Former AA sponsor from 2023 cycle, lost contact.
Stressors/problems:: Social isolation post-job-loss. Drift from former sober peer group. No current peer-recovery network.
Recent changes:: Has not contacted former sponsor in 12+ months. Sober friends drifted as drinking escalated in 2024.
Changes desired:: Reconnect with former sponsor; build new sober peer network through structured group.
7. Cultural/Ethnic
Strengths/support:: Identifies as Hispanic/Latino. Strong cultural value placed on family ties (familismo).
Stressors/problems:: Cultural shame around mental health and substance use. Internalized 'be a man, handle it yourself'
narrative.
Beliefs/practices to incorporate into therapy:: Family-systems framing welcomed. Spanish-language psychoeducation
materials acceptable. Open to culturally-aware peer matching.
8. Spiritual/Religious
Strengths/support:: Raised Catholic. Faith was a source of comfort in childhood; mother and grandmother were practicing.
Stressors/problems:: Currently disconnected from practice. Reports guilt and shame around substance use as a barrier to
returning to church.
Beliefs/practices to incorporate into therapy:: Open to facility chaplaincy if available. Open to AA/NA frameworks that
incorporate higher-power language without requiring it.
Recent changes:: Has not attended Mass in 4+ years. Grandmother (primary spiritual influence) died in 2022.
Changes desired:: Wants to 'find some peace' but not actively pursuing a specific practice at this time.
9. Legal
History:: No prior arrests or convictions.
Status/impact/stressors:: Pending DUI charge (2026-04-12). Court date TBD; assigned public defender. May lose driver's
license. Stressor weighing heavily on treatment ambivalence and willingness to engage.
10. Education
Strengths:: High school graduate. Completed 18 credits of community college coursework.
Weaknesses:: Did not complete associate's degree. Reports difficulty with sustained concentration since 2019 mTBI,
exacerbated by current substance use.
11. Employment/Vocational
Strengths/support:: 5-year tenure in warehouse logistics (2020–2026). Considered reliable when sober.
Stressors/problems:: Unemployed x 6 weeks. Terminated for intoxication at work (workplace breathalyzer policy violation).
Income loss is a major stressor. No unemployment income — termination was 'for cause.' Identity disruption: "I'm not used
to not working."
12. Military
Current impact:: No military service history.
13. Leisure/Recreational
Strengths/support:: Previously enjoyed watching basketball and walking in the neighborhood.
Recent changes:: Has not engaged in leisure activities x 6 months — substance use has crowded everything else out.
Changes desired:: Wants to 'get back into walking' as a wellness practice during/after treatment.
14. Physical Health
Summary of health:: Active: uncontrolled essential hypertension, suspected alcoholic hepatitis (not biopsy-confirmed),
remote mild TBI (2019). No current primary care relationship. Last PCP visit 2024 for naltrexone prescription.
Physical factors affecting mental condition:: Severe sleep deprivation (<2 h/night for several days pre-admission).
Withdrawal physiology (autonomic arousal, tremor) directly affecting cognition, mood, and concentration. Hepatic
dysfunction may affect medication metabolism — clinical relevance for benzo taper and any future SSRI/SNRI selection.
Vitals (BP, HR, RR, temp, SpO2):: BP 158/96; HR 104; RR 18; T 99.1°F; SpO2 97%.
Current medications (name, dose, frequency, prescriber):: None at admission. Was prescribed lisinopril 10 mg PO daily by
PCP in 2024 for HTN; non-adherent x 18 months. To be re-initiated on admission day 4 per inpatient medical orders.
Allergies:: No known drug allergies (NKDA).
Recent labs (date, panel, results):: Hepatic panel 2026-05-04: AST 142 U/L (ref 10–40), ALT 98 U/L (ref 7–56), GGT 312 U/L (ref
9–48), total bilirubin 1.4 mg/dL (ref 0.1–1.2) — consistent with alcohol-related hepatic injury. UDS 2026-05-04: POSITIVE for
ethanol, benzodiazepines, cannabinoids; NEGATIVE for opioids, cocaine, amphetamines.
15. Chemical Use History
Summary of use:: Polysubstance: heavy daily alcohol (4 years), daily illicit alprazolam (18 months), recreational cannabis
(years). Denies opioid, stimulant, and hallucinogen use; UDS corroborates. Active alcohol withdrawal at intake (CIWA-Ar =
12); benzodiazepine withdrawal anticipated.
Patient’s perception of problem:: Minimizes severity: "I drink a lot but it's not that bad." Attributes ED visit to "just a fall, not
the drinking." Acknowledges alprazolam use is "getting out of hand" but does not connect it to the withdrawal-anticipation
finding. Ambivalent about treatment: "I'm here because my brother said so."
Per-substance breakdown (alcohol, sedative-hypnotics, cannabis, opioids, stimulants, other) — for each:
first/last use, route, frequency, amounts, withdrawal hx, prior tx:: • Alcohol: first use age 16; pattern ~14 standard
drinks/day x 4 years (vodka, beer); last use 2026-05-03; route oral; withdrawal history — Multiple episodes; one prior ED
visit for seizure precaution; prior treatment — 2023 outpatient, 2024 naltrexone trial.
• Alprazolam (Xanax): first use age 32; pattern 1 mg PO daily x 18 months (originally Rx, now illicit); last use 2026-05-03;
route oral; withdrawal history — Anticipated; not yet manifest at intake; prior treatment — None.
• Cannabis: first use age 17; pattern 2-3 joints per week, recreational; last use 2026-04-28; route inhaled; withdrawal history
— None reported; prior treatment — None.
• Opioids: DENIES current or past opioid use. COWS recorded as N/A; documented to demonstrate negative-finding
handling
AUDIT-C (date, items, total, interpretation):: AUDIT-C administered 2026-05-04: frequency 4, typical quantity 4, heavy
episodic 3 — total 11 (positive, high risk).
DAST-10 (date, items, total, interpretation):: DAST-10 administered 2026-05-04: total 7 (substantial level, indicates intensive
assessment and treatment indicated).
16. Counseling/Prior Treatment History
Summary of prior treatment:: 2023 — Outpatient individual counseling, 6 weeks at community mental health center. Self-
discontinued. 2024 — PCP-prescribed naltrexone 50 mg PO daily x 3 months; non-adherent and discontinued. No prior
residential or inpatient SUD treatment.
Benefits of previous treatment:: Brief reduction in drinking (~30% by self-report) during the 2023 counseling cycle.
Setbacks of previous treatment:: Self-discontinued before completing planned course in 2023. Naltrexone non-adherence
with no follow-up. No prior MAT, no prior recovery group attendance.
17. Past Psychiatric History
Prior psychiatric diagnoses (DSM-5-TR / ICD-10):: • Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent, moderate (ICD-10 F33.1; DSM-5-TR
296.32; onset 2019)
• Generalized Anxiety Disorder (ICD-10 F41.1; DSM-5-TR 300.02; onset 2020)
Psychiatric hospitalizations (year, facility, reason, duration):: • 2021 — Memorial Behavioral Health — Suicidal ideation,
voluntary 72-hour hold
Prior psychiatric medications (drug, dose, dates, prescriber, response):: • Sertraline 100mg — 2020-2022 — Self-
discontinued
• Alprazolam 0.5mg PRN — 2023 — Escalated to daily then illicit
Self-harm history:: One episode of superficial cutting age 22; no attempts; no recent ideation with plan
Prior suicide attempts (lifetime):: None.
18. Mental Status Exam
Appearance:: Disheveled, appropriate for age, malodorous of alcohol on arrival
Behavior / psychomotor:: Cooperative, mild psychomotor restlessness
Speech:: Normal rate, mildly pressured
Mood (client-reported):: Depressed and anxious
Affect (clinician-observed):: Constricted, congruent with mood
Thought process:: Linear and goal-directed
Thought content:: Passive death wish; no active SI/HI; no delusions
Perception:: No hallucinations
Cognition / orientation:: Alert and oriented x3; MoCA deferred due to withdrawal
Insight:: Limited — minimizes severity of substance use
Judgment:: Impaired — recent fall, continued use despite consequences
Standardized screening — PHQ-9 (date, items, total):: PHQ-9 administered 2026-05-04: anhedonia 3, depressed mood 3,
sleep 3, fatigue 2, appetite 2, self-worth 2, concentration 2, psychomotor 1, suicidal ideation 0 — total 18 (moderately
severe).
Standardized screening — GAD-7 (date, items, total):: GAD-7 administered 2026-05-04: nervousness 3, uncontrollable worry
3, excessive worry 2, trouble relaxing 2, restlessness 2, irritability 2, fear 1 — total 15 (severe).
19. Risk Assessment
Suicide risk — C-SSRS (date, items, interpretation):: C-SSRS administered 2026-05-04: Q1 no, Q2 YES ("I sometimes wish I
weren't here"), Q3 no, Q4 no, Q5 no, Q6 no lifetime suicidal behavior. Risk: low-intensity passive ideation; no active
SI/plan/intent.
Homicidal ideation:: Denies. No ideation, plan, intent, or lifetime history.
Withdrawal risk — CIWA-Ar (date, items, total):: CIWA-Ar administered 2026-05-04 14:30: nausea/vomiting 2, tremor 3,
sweats 2, anxiety 2, agitation 1, tactile 0, auditory 0, visual 0, headache 1, orientation 1 — total 12 (moderate).
Withdrawal risk — COWS (date, items, total, or N/A):: COWS: not administered. Patient denies any opioid use; UDS negative
for opioids. Documented for completeness.
Violence / aggression risk:: Low. No history of interpersonal violence; no current threats or ideation.
Overall risk level:: Moderate — driven by withdrawal severity (CIWA-Ar = 12), passive suicidal ideation (C-SSRS Q2-positive),
and unstable recovery environment.
Safety plan / precautions:: Inpatient monitoring with CIWA-Ar q4h; nursing line of sight if CIWA ≥ 15. Fall precautions in
place. Suicide precautions: standard observation given passive ideation without plan/intent. Re-administer C-SSRS prior to
any level-of-care change per NPSG.15.01.01.
20. Diagnosis
Primary diagnosis (DSM-5-TR / ICD-10):: Alcohol Use Disorder, severe, with withdrawal (F10.232; DSM-5-TR 303.90).
Secondary diagnosis (DSM-5-TR / ICD-10):: Sedative, Hypnotic, or Anxiolytic Use Disorder, severe (F13.20; DSM-5-TR 304.10).
Tertiary diagnosis (DSM-5-TR / ICD-10):: Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent episode, moderate (F33.1; DSM-5-TR 296.32).
Differential / rule-outs:: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) is a co-occurring consideration, but anxiety symptoms may be
substantially driven by current withdrawal physiology — reassess 2 weeks post-stabilization. Recommended level of care
on admission: ASAM 3.7 — Medically Monitored Intensive Inpatient, driven by Dim 1 (active polysubstance withdrawal) and
Dim 5 (unsafe recovery environment).
21. Treatment Plan
Goal 1 (domain, goal, target date, measure):: Domain: Substance use. Goal: Achieve and maintain 30 days of abstinence
from alcohol and benzodiazepines. Target date: 2026-06-03. Measure: Daily breathalyzer, weekly UDS.
Goal 2 (domain, goal, target date, measure):: Domain: Mental health. Goal: Reduce PHQ-9 score from 18 to <10 by 60 days.
Target date: 2026-07-03. Measure: Bi-weekly PHQ-9.
Goal 3 (domain, goal, target date, measure):: Domain: Recovery environment. Goal: Identify and engage one sober support
person and one alternate housing option. Target date: 2026-05-25. Measure: Social-work documentation.
Interventions (list with frequency):: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) — 3x/week individual
• Motivational Interviewing (MI) — woven across sessions
• Librium taper, gabapentin adjunct, thiamine
• Psychiatric medication evaluation for MDD/GAD (in week 2)
• Case-management for housing and DUI court navigation
Expected outcomes:: • Stable medical withdrawal within 7 days
• PHQ-9 < 10 by week 8
• Step-down to PHP/IOP by week 2 if Dims 1 and 2 resolve
Discharge / step-down criteria:: Step down to PHP (ASAM 2.5) when: (a) CIWA-Ar < 5 for 48 hours, (b) BP controlled on
lisinopril, (c) sober housing option identified, (d) C-SSRS re-administered and stable. Target step-down date: 2026-05-15.

from a legitimate 0.5 mg PRN prescription to illicit 1 mg daily. Cannabis: recreational, 2–3x weekly. Acute alcohol withdrawal
currently moderate (CIWA-Ar = 12). Benzodiazepine withdrawal anticipated but not yet manifest. Depressive and anxious
symptoms have been continuously present x 4 years with worsening since job loss 6 weeks ago.
Was there a clear time when Sx worsened?
Yes — substance use and depressive symptoms escalated sharply 6 weeks ago following job loss (terminated for
intoxication at work). Acute withdrawal began approximately 36 hours prior to admission after a forced cut-down attempt
(no alcohol available at home over the weekend).
Family mental health history:
Father with alcohol use disorder; mother with depression

counseling_prior_treatment_history.title: Counseling/Prior Treatment History
counseling_prior_treatment_history.text:
Summary of prior treatment:: 2023 — Outpatient individual counseling, 6 weeks at community mental health center. Self-
discontinued. 2024 — PCP-prescribed naltrexone 50 mg PO daily x 3 months; non-adherent and discontinued. No prior
residential or inpatient SUD treatment.
Benefits of previous treatment:: Brief reduction in drinking (~30% by self-report) during the 2023 counseling cycle.
Setbacks of previous treatment:: Self-discontinued before completing planned course in 2023. Naltrexone non-adherence
with no follow-up. No prior MAT, no prior recovery group attendance.

current_family_and_significant_relations.title: Current Family and Significant Relationships
current_family_and_significant_relations.text:
Strengths/support:: Brother Daniel willing to engage; provided transportation to ED.
Stressors/problems:: Brother is an active substance user (alcohol, cannabis). Patient is housing-dependent on the brother.
No partner, no children. Parents live out of state; minimal contact.
Recent changes:: Job loss 6 weeks ago; pending DUI charge. Brother delivered ultimatum about housing.
Changes desired:: Stable sober housing; restored autonomy; reconnect with mother.
Comment on family circumstances:: Father with untreated alcohol use disorder. Mother with treated major depression.
Patient is the younger of two siblings.

Patient meets DSM-5-TR criteria for Alcohol Use Disorder, severe (≥6 criteria endorsed: tolerance, withdrawal, hazardous
use, continued use despite social/occupational consequences, time spent obtaining/using, unsuccessful cut-down
attempts); Sedative-Hypnotic Use Disorder, severe (alprazolam); and Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent, moderate
